plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in Pretoria turn lavender-purple as clouds of trumpet-shaped blossoms open. The fallen flowers carpet pavements and cars in violet. The tree is a spring spectacle in the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September through October, with blossoms often lingering into November
plants.funFact: Jacarandas come from South America, but Pretoria has so many that it is nicknamed the Jacaranda City. Locals joke that a flower landing on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy evergreen shrub opens delicate, often lightly scented blooms just as other gardens are fading. Its single or semi-double flowers have bright golden stamens at the center. They light up autumn borders and hedges.
plants.bloomingSeason: Begins in October and peaks in November, with some cultivars flowering into December or later
plants.location: Southeastern United States, where the Lowcountry gardens of South Carolina start their display in late October
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are native to Japan. They are the early-season camellias, opening weeks before their showier cousin Camellia japonica.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: Glossy golden goblets rise straight from bare ground, looking like crocuses dipped in sunshine. They appear with the first autumn rains, before the leaves have fully grown. They bring a burst of yellow to dry Mediterranean hillsides and rock gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to October, occasionally into November
plants.location: Mediterranean region, including Greece, Turkey and the Levant
plants.funFact: Despite the name, this bulb is not a true crocus or a daffodil. It belongs to the amaryllis family and is often linked to the 'lily of the field' mentioned in ancient texts.
